title: 2010 AMC 10A Problem 21
statement: The polynomial \[x^3-ax^2+bx-2010\] has three positive integer zeros. What is the smallest possible value of \(a?\)

solutions.text:
Let the roots be positive integers \(r\le s\le t.\) By Vieta’s formulas, \(rst=2010\) and \(a=r+s+t.\)

Since \(2010=2\cdot3\cdot5\cdot67,\) one root must be divisible by \(67.\) If that root is larger than \(67,\) then it is at least \(134,\) which is already worse than the construction below.

Thus take \(t=67\) and minimize \(r+s\) with \(rs=30.\) The factor pair with smallest sum is \(5\) and \(6,\) so \(a=5+6+67=78.\)

Thus, A is the correct answer.
hints: The roots multiply to \(2010\) and sum to \(a\)
Put \(67\) alone, then split \(30\) into two factors with smallest sum
